worlds.name: Ossara
worlds.description: The green Reach, and the one everybody starts in. Ilvaro's country: worked land, short roads, and a gate in the middle of town that has not opened in living memory.

zones.name: The Terraces
zones.description: Farm shelves stepping down the hill south of Gatetown. Where everyone learns which end of a billhook is which.

zones.name: Brackenfell
zones.description: Scrub woodland and old quarry between the farms and the rim. Firewood, charcoal, and a toll nobody agreed to.

zones.name: The Rimwalk
zones.description: Where the land stops. Sulveth's ground, and the road out of Ossara.

itemTemplates.name: a fallen road marker
itemTemplates.description: A shaped stone the length of a forearm, cut with the old road mark. It has been face down in the gorse long enough for moss to take one side.

itemTemplates.name: somebody's keepsake
itemTemplates.description: A wedding ring, a whittled bird, a key to a door that is no longer anywhere. Every one of them used to belong to somebody, and says so.

itemTemplates.name: a shard of gate-stone
itemTemplates.description: Dark stone, cool in a way the afternoon cannot fix. The broken face is not rough. It is as smooth as the outside, which means it was never one piece.

itemTemplates.name: an unproven oathmaul
itemTemplates.description: Head like a milestone, haft the length of a person. It was made to stop something. Newly made and honest about it. Vesh will not pretend this is finished.

itemTemplates.name: an unproven hearthcenser
itemTemplates.description: A censer on a chain, weighted for swinging and never once used for incense. Newly made and honest about it. Vesh will not pretend this is finished.

itemTemplates.name: an unproven stormrod
itemTemplates.description: Bronze wound with wire that stands the hair up on your arm when the weather turns. Newly made and honest about it. Vesh will not pretend this is finished.

itemTemplates.name: an unproven quiet knife
itemTemplates.description: It does not catch the light. Somebody took a great deal of trouble over that. Newly made and honest about it. Vesh will not pretend this is finished.

itemTemplates.name: a banked ember
itemTemplates.description: It is not warm and it has not gone out. Vesh keeps a jar of them and will not say where the first one came from.

mobTemplates.name: a barn rat
mobTemplates.description: Fat on spilled grain and entirely uninterested in you until you are between it and the sack.

mobTemplates.name: a terrace crow
mobTemplates.description: One of the flock that works the terraces. It has learned that people carry food and that people are slow.

mobTemplates.name: a scrub dog
mobTemplates.description: Nobody owns it and it does not hunt alone. There are always others in the gorse.

mobTemplates.name: a hedge thief
mobTemplates.description: Working the field edges for anything unattended. Comes off the wall swinging a billhook and is genuinely surprised when that does not settle it.

mobTemplates.name: a road cutpurse
mobTemplates.description: Light, fast, and out of Gatetown a week ahead of a question they did not want to answer.

mobTemplates.name: a bracken boar
mobTemplates.description: Waist high at the shoulder and built entirely for going forward. It commits early and it takes a long moment to turn.

mobTemplates.name: a hill toller
mobTemplates.description: One of the crew charging a toll on a road nobody gave them. Well equipped, badly led, and very committed to the fiction.

mobTemplates.name: a gorse lurcher
mobTemplates.description: Long, low and the colour of dead bracken. It does not chase. It waits where the path narrows and it gets a grip on you.

mobTemplates.name: one of the left behind
mobTemplates.description: It is a person shape and it is carrying something, and it will not put the thing down. Sulveth keeps what is lost. She does not always keep it still.

mobTemplates.name: the Unclaimed
mobTemplates.description: Taller than the others and put together out of more than one person's belongings. It has been at the rim longer than the marker stones have.

mobTemplates.name: Vesh, who follows the gates
mobTemplates.description: A smith with a travelling anvil and no forge, who has been at every crossing anyone can remember and looks no older in any of the stories. She works for materials and will not take coin.

emotes.text: turns a piece over and puts it back in the bag unfinished
says, 'I do not sell. Bring me something and I will make it better.'
sets an anvil down that nobody saw her carrying

mobTemplates.name: Sesk, who walks the terraces
mobTemplates.description: She checks the dry-stone walls one shelf at a time, all year, and can tell you which season each repair is from.

emotes.text: sets a fallen stone back into a wall without breaking stride
says, 'Wall holds the soil. Soil holds the wall. Do not let either start.'

greeting: 'Walk the path, not the wall. The wall is older than the path and it is not for you.'
'Autumn repair, that one. You can tell by the moss.'

mobTemplates.name: Keeper Vess of Sulveth's stone
mobTemplates.description: She keeps the blank stone at the rim, and has done for thirty years. She is not gloomy about it and has no patience for anyone who is.

emotes.text: sets a found thing on the stone and writes nothing beside it
says, 'Sulveth keeps what is lost. She does not give it back. Those are two facts, not one.'

rooms.title: The High Shelf
rooms.description:
The first of the terraces, and the widest. Dry-stone walls hold the soil in long green steps down the slope, each one a little narrower than the last.

A hoe leans against the wall where somebody left it, and the row beside it is half done.

rooms.title: The Drying Frames
rooms.description:
Racks of split hazel, chest high, hung with beans and onion tops in the sun. The frames are re-tied every spring and none of the knots match.

Something has been at the low end of the third rack. There are droppings, and a hole in the wall behind it that was not put there by a mason.

rooms.title: The Water Race
rooms.description:
A stone channel a hand deep runs along the shelf, carrying water from the river out to the far end and letting it fall shelf to shelf through cut notches.

The notches have wooden gates in them. Which gates are open is somebody's whole job, and arguing about it is most of the village's entertainment.

rooms.title: The Cellar Mouth
rooms.description:
A door set flat into the hillside with two stone steps down to it, propped open with a rock because the hinge has gone. Cold air comes out of it even at noon.

Root vegetables go in here in autumn and come out all winter. Something else has been going in and out year round.

rooms.title: The Root Cellar
rooms.description:
Earth walls, timber props, and sacking laid over the floor. Turnips and beet in slatted bins along one side, most of a barrel of apples along the other.

Every sack at the far end has been opened from underneath.

rooms.title: The Lower Rows
rooms.description:
Beans on strings, three shelves of them, running the whole width of the terrace. The strings are tied to hazel poles and the poles lean where the ground has crept.

It is the best cover on the whole hillside and everything on the hillside knows it.

rooms.title: The Goat Fold
rooms.description:
A pen of hurdles against the retaining wall, holding nine goats who have all worked out that hurdles can be leaned on. The tenth is somewhere else.

A boy is supposed to be here. His stick is here.

rooms.title: The Orchard Shelf
rooms.description:
Twenty apple trees on the widest of the lower terraces, pruned hard and standing in grass that is kept short by the goats when the goats are meant to be here.

Windfalls lie under every tree. The crows have had the best of them and are not sorry.

rooms.title: The Beehives
rooms.description:
Six straw skeps on a stone bench, facing the morning sun, each with its own slate roof weighted down by a rock.

Somebody has told the bees something recently. The rag tied to the third skep is the village's way of doing it, and it is fresh.

rooms.title: The Terrace Foot
rooms.description:
The bottom of the worked land. The last wall is twice the height of the others and the ground past it is scrub going to gorse.

A stile crosses the wall here, worn hollow in the middle by two generations of people going out to Brackenfell for wood and coming back with less than they hoped.

rooms.title: The Stile Path
rooms.description:
A trodden line through waist-high bracken, wide enough for one and used by two. The terraces are a green staircase behind you and the scrub closes over the path ahead.

Somebody has cut a blaze into the third birch along. There is another further on, and then they stop.

rooms.title: The Birch Stand
rooms.description:
Thin birches close together, all of them leaning the same way, with light coming down through them in bars. The ground is clean underneath and quiet to walk on.

This is where Gatetown gets its firewood, and the stumps are cut low and level by people who intend to come back.

rooms.title: The Gorse Run
rooms.description:
Gorse over head height on both sides and a path through it barely a shoulder wide. The spines catch at everything and the flowers smell absurdly of coconut.

There are runs pushed through the base of it at knee height, going somewhere else.

rooms.title: The Thorn Hollow
rooms.description:
A dip where the gorse gives out and blackthorn takes over, so dense at the edges that the middle is bare ground.

Bones in the middle, small ones, picked clean and dragged into no particular arrangement.

rooms.title: The Wet Hollow
rooms.description:
A boggy dip full of sedge and standing water that never quite drains, crossed by three planks laid end to end on stones.

The middle plank moves when you step on it. Everyone knows. Nobody has fixed it.

rooms.title: The Alder Carr
rooms.description:
Alder growing straight out of the water on stilts of root, close enough together that you pick your way rather than walk.

Whatever lives in here has learned that people are loud and slow and only come through in daylight.

rooms.title: The Charcoal Burn
rooms.description:
A flat circle of bare scorched earth twenty feet across, with a shallow pit at the middle and a ring of turf sods stacked to one side.

The burn is cold. The sods have been stacked ready for a month and nobody has come back to set it.

rooms.title: The Old Quarry
rooms.description:
A bite taken out of the hillside, three storeys of pale rock face with a floor of chips and puddles. Every wall in Gatetown came out of here.

The tool marks stop halfway up one face, mid-course, as though the day ended and did not start again.

rooms.title: The Quarry Shelf
rooms.description:
A ledge halfway up the quarry face, reached by a ramp of spoil, wide enough for a cart and once used by several.

Somebody is camping up here. The fire is banked, not out, and there is more gear than one person needs.

rooms.title: The Cutting Bank
rooms.description:
The old road runs through a cutting here, banks of red earth and root above head height on both sides, and it is exactly as good an ambush as it looks.

The road surface is still sound. Whoever laid it was better at this than anyone living.

rooms.title: The Toll Post
rooms.description:
A pole across the road on two forked stakes, with a plank nailed to it reading TOLL in paint that has run. Nobody has any authority to put it there.

The crew who did are camped where they can see both ways along the cutting, which is the one part of this they have thought through.

rooms.title: The Boar Wallow
rooms.description:
A churned patch of black mud twenty feet across, ringed with rubbed-smooth trees and smelling like the underside of a wet dog.

The tracks going in are deep and splayed. Nothing small made these.

rooms.title: The Long Bracken
rooms.description:
Bracken taller than a person for as far as you can see, with the path a green tunnel through it and the sky a strip overhead.

You cannot see anything off the path. Anything off the path can hear exactly where you are.

rooms.title: The Far Blaze
rooms.description:
The last of the cut blazes, on a birch that has grown around it until the mark is a knuckle of scar tissue.

Past here the bracken thins, the soil goes to grit, and the ground begins its long tilt towards the rim.

rooms.title: The Thinning
rooms.description:
The bracken gives up in stages. First the tall stuff, then the low, then a scatter of gorse in grit, and then grass so short it looks grazed by something nobody has seen.

The ground tilts. Not steeply. Just enough that walking is easier than stopping.

rooms.title: The Picnic Stones
rooms.description:
Three flat slabs dragged into a rough triangle, generations ago, by people who wanted somewhere to sit and look at the edge.

The stones are scratched all over with names and dates. The most recent is from this spring. So is the ring of ash beside it.

Far out past the edge, on a clear afternoon, there are shapes in the distance that could be land. They never resolve, however long you look, and the haze between never quite behaves like haze.

rooms.title: The Watch Stone
rooms.description:
A single upright of the pale local rock, twice the height of a person, standing where the ground begins to fall away in earnest. It is not one of the markers - it is older and it is not cut with anything.

Someone has kept the turf clear around its base. Recently, and with a blade.

rooms.title: The Marker Line
rooms.description:
Shaped stones set into the turf every thirty paces, running out towards the edge, each cut with a mark that is not any letter Gatetown uses.

Half of them are down. The ones still standing lean the same way, which is not the way the wind comes from.

rooms.title: The Gorse Tongue
rooms.description:
A last spit of gorse running out along a spur of higher ground, thinning as it goes until the bushes are separate and stunted.

The path narrows to a single line between two of them. It is the only way along the spur and everything using this ground knows it.

rooms.title: The Spur End
rooms.description:
The spur runs out. Grit, then turf, then nothing - the ground ends in a clean line with roots and soil showing in cross-section.

People have thrown things off here for a long time to watch what happens. Nothing happens. They do not fall and they do not stay.

Far out past the edge, on a clear afternoon, there are shapes in the distance that could be land. They never resolve, however long you look, and the haze between never quite behaves like haze.

rooms.title: The Keeper's Stone
rooms.description:
A waist-high block of pale rock with a flat top, standing alone where the marker line bends. Nothing is written on it and nothing ever has been.

Things are laid on it. A shoe, a comb, a bundle of letters gone to pulp. Nobody takes them, and nobody puts them anywhere else either.

rooms.title: The Cairn Field
rooms.description:
Forty or fifty stone piles, none of them tall, spread across a shallow bowl of ground. Some are neat. Most have come apart.

They are not graves. Every one of them has a hollow in the top where something was meant to be set, and every hollow is empty.

rooms.title: The Lost Way
rooms.description:
The old road again, or what it becomes out here: two ruts in the turf running dead straight at the edge, with the marker stones keeping pace on either side.

It does not curve away. Whoever built it was going somewhere that used to be there.

Far out past the edge, on a clear afternoon, there are shapes in the distance that could be land. They never resolve, however long you look, and the haze between never quite behaves like haze.

rooms.title: The Forgetting Ground
rooms.description:
The turf here is wrong in a way that takes a moment. It is uncropped, unwalked, and the marker stones stop twenty paces short of it on both sides.

Things stand about in it. They were people, and they are carrying what they were carrying, and they have not put any of it down.

Far out past the edge, on a clear afternoon, there are shapes in the distance that could be land. They never resolve, however long you look, and the haze between never quite behaves like haze.

rooms.title: The Rim Gate
rooms.description:
A ring of dark stone, twin to the dead one in Gatetown's yard, standing at the very edge with nothing behind it.

This one works. It has always worked. This season it does not, and the difference is not visible: it stands exactly as it stood, and what was through it is not.

Whatever should be on the other side is not there. Not dark, not distance - the same nothing as everywhere else past the edge, arriving where a place used to.

exits.refusalMessage: The ring is cold and the air inside it does not move. Something here has not been told your name.

rooms.title: The Last Marker
rooms.description:
The final stone of the line, out past the gate, standing at an angle on ground that gives underfoot in a way ground should not.

It is the only marker still carrying what it was meant to carry: a shard of the same dark stone the gates are cut from, socketed into its head, and warm.

Far out past the edge, on a clear afternoon, there are shapes in the distance that could be land. They never resolve, however long you look, and the haze between never quite behaves like haze.

quests.name: The Road Out
quests.summary: Recover four fallen road markers from the Rimwalk.
quests.description: Deacon Pell has worked out that the gate stopped when the marker line came down, which is either the whole answer or a coincidence. He would like the stones back up either way.

dialogue.giverOffer: Pell has a map with more crossings-out than lines. '<The stones> came down and the gate stopped. In that order. I am not saying it is the reason. I am saying nobody has checked.'
dialogue.giverInProgress: 'Four. Any four. They all weigh the same amount of nothing to Ilvaro and rather a lot to you, I imagine.'
dialogue.giverComplete: 'Still up there, are they? They are not getting lighter.'
dialogue.turninReady: He turns one over twice. 'Right. So they are cut on both faces. Nobody mentioned that. Take a rest, and then would you mind terribly—'

quests.name: What Sulveth Keeps
quests.summary: Collect six keepsakes from the left behind.
quests.description: The things standing about on the forgetting ground are carrying what they were carrying. Pell wants them back. He has not thought past that.

dialogue.giverOffer: 'They are holding things,' Pell says, and stops, and starts again. 'Somebody is missing those <things>. That is all I am confident about.'
dialogue.giverInProgress: 'Six should do. Take them to the Keeper, not to me. She will know what they are. I will only guess and be wrong in front of you.'
dialogue.giverComplete: 'Six. And do not sort them. I will sort them.'
dialogue.turninReady: Vess lays them out on the blank stone without hurrying. 'These went first,' she says. 'The stones went second. The gate went third. He has the order backwards and the right idea.'

quests.name: A Gate Does Not Break
quests.summary: Take the shard from the Unclaimed to Keeper Vess.
quests.description: The last marker still carries its shard, and the Unclaimed is standing over it. Vess wants the stone, and she has decided you have earned the sentence that comes with it.

dialogue.giverOffer: Vess does not look up. '<Last stone> still has its piece. The big one is standing on it. I am seventy and I am not going to be the one to ask it to move.'
dialogue.giverInProgress: 'One shard. Out past the ring, where the ground gives. Mind your footing and mind the thing that is already there.'
dialogue.giverComplete: 'Still standing there, is it. Yes. It does that.'
dialogue.turninReady: She turns the shard so the smooth broken face catches the light. 'A gate does not break,' she says. 'It forgets. Somebody stopped saying the name of the other side and it stopped being able to find it.' She presses the shard into your hand. 'It knows you now. Go and see what is left of Grask, and mind what looks back.'

quests.name: The Oathmaul, unproven
quests.description: Vesh works for materials and not for coin, and she has decided what she is making for you before you asked.

dialogue.giverOffer: Vesh looks at you rather than at your hands. 'You are a Warden. I know what a Warden needs and I have known for a long time.' She sets down a bag. '<Three embers>. The big one at the rim has them - it has been carrying them longer than I have been walking.'
dialogue.giverInProgress: 'Three. They do not go out and they do not warm anything. Bring them.'
dialogue.giverComplete: 'When it has been through something. Not before.'
dialogue.turninReady: She works without hurrying and hands it back. 'Better,' she says. That is the whole of her opinion and it is worth more than it sounds.

configurations.description: The Reaches as designed in docs/WORLD.md. New characters begin in Gatetown, at the gate that has not opened in living memory.
